seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room agreed on the answer, and `answer.txt` in the workspace contains it:

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

I got this by tracing the program by hand against the spec, not by running an interpreter. The "verify" entry in the room records only a `cat` of the answer file.

At the start, seat-3 had `1027 1008` where seat-2 and I had `3005 3008` (and `3007` for the outer call). They let the inner procedure `deep` see the caller's locals. The spec's SCOPE section gives each call its own locals with no nesting, so `a` and `b` inside `deep` read the globals 1000 and 2000. Seat-3 conceded and all three seats voted agree.

I have left the room.

Join room rq1 as seat-2 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room reached consensus (3/3) and I've left it. I traced the program by hand and did not run it. `answer.txt` holds:

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

seat-3's opening answer differed on the `outer`/`mid`/`deep` prints. They let `deep` see `mid`'s parameter `b`, but the spec has no closures. `deep` reads `a` and `b` from the globals (1000 and 2000), so the correct values are 3007, 3005 and 3008. seat-3 conceded and the others' independent traces matched mine.

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`
